page: Amazon Web Services c5d.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core.

This instance type includes 200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, which serves as high-speed instance store volumes. Network performance is characterized by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. There are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled with this instance.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across most standard workloads. The server achieves average ratings in multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and software compilation. However, single-core stress-ng performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are rated as weak. LLM inference capabilities are limited, with prompt processing for a 7B model falling into the poor category. The hardware configuration is suitable for compute-intensive workloads that benefit from low-latency local storage, such as batch processing, distributed analytics, and moderate database operations.
description: Amazon Web Services c5d.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 3.4 GHz. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory and 200 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Performance benchmarks place this server in the average tier for multi-core CPU tasks, memory bandwidth, and software compilation, though it exhibits weaker performance in single-core operations and large-model LLM inference. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring a balance of dedicated compute power and high-speed local temporary storage, making it suitable for batch processing, web serving, and distributed data pipelines.
